scores.accuracy_concern: Hutchins data are SWOG trials from 1993 to 1996 and must be dated in the post; the claim that the gap persists rests on Ludmir 2019, which is unverified; the 63% comparator is the share of US cancer patients aged 65 or over, not people with cancer worldwide.
scores.sharpen: Pair the 1990s figure with a verified recent analysis so the post shows whether the gap persists, and end on the one-line baseline-table check; choose this or C20-05, not both plus C20-07.

scores.accuracy_concern: Boyd 2005 applied US guidelines to a hypothetical patient; confirm 12 medicines (and dose count) from full text and do not present it as NICE; Dumbreck's 133 are potential interactions between guideline recommendations, not observed harms; 'No trial tested this combination' is an inference and should be worded as one.
scores.sharpen: Put the UK finding (Dumbreck or Hughes) beside Boyd so UK readers cannot dismiss it as American, and close on one concrete step: review the whole list against the person's top two priorities. Check against C06 polypharmacy picks.

scores.accuracy_concern: Taylor 2012's 6% may be a share of all 434 articles rather than of the studies that excluded people with cognitive impairment, so the draft opening may use the wrong denominator; Adults with Incapacity (Scotland) Act s51 and the Clinical Trials Regulations legal-representative rules must be worded from the legislation itself.
scores.sharpen: Confirm the denominator for the 6% and replace the three legal boxes with one precise sentence per jurisdiction, keeping the inclusion argument labelled as ethical judgement.

scores.accuracy_concern: Hensel's 2 to 4 point reliable-change range applies to cognitively normal people over 75 retested at 18-month intervals at 90% confidence and does not transfer to people with dementia or other intervals; KDIGO 2024 may not keep the 2012 'certain drop' wording; the MMSE and family-account point partly repeats E015.
scores.sharpen: Pick one measurement, probably eGFR in older people, give one verified threshold with its conditions, and drop the second half-explained rule.

scores.accuracy_concern: Cherubini's two categories overlap (a trial can have both an age limit and poorly justified criteria), so 'more common than upper age limits' should be two separate percentages; the checklist items 'living in a care home' and 'unable to attend visits' must appear in the cited reviews or be dropped; the data are 2008 registrations.
scores.sharpen: Anchor it in one named trial's exclusion list with the Cherubini percentages as context, and run it instead of, not alongside, C20-01 and C20-07.

scores.accuracy_concern: Wording must match Glass 1998 ('discordance' among hypothetical, experimental and enacted function) rather than 'consistent disagreement'; the ICF capacity and performance qualifiers are defined for a standard versus current environment; the self-report versus performance agreement claim still needs a source.
scores.sharpen: Anchor it in the discharge decision: the home visit or the carer's account of 7am is the 'does do' measurement, and the discharge letter should say which one the score records.

scores.accuracy_concern: Gross 2002 describes trials from 1999 to 2000, before the CONSORT flow diagram was routine, so the 52% figure should not be presented as current practice; the 'assessed for eligibility' number often counts only pre-screened people, so the box can understate selection; the 68-per-enrolled figure needs checking.
scores.sharpen: Use one recent trial in older people with a verified screened-to-randomised ratio and ask one question of it, instead of old reporting statistics.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 10-of-14 figure comes from trials of information provision after stroke only and should not be generalised to all stroke research without Townend 2007 or similar; 'about a third' needs a primary epidemiological source; 'many can decide for themselves with accessible information' needs its own support (Jayes and Palmer unverified).
scores.sharpen: Keep the scope of the 10-of-14 figure explicit, show one verified accessible-format consent sentence beside the standard one, and name one tested consent support tool.

scores.accuracy_concern: The premise that poor recruitment is 'often put down to reluctance' is asserted without a source; Forsat's percentages are shares of studies reporting a barrier, not shares of people; several checklist items (companion costs, large print, hearing support) are not in the review.
scores.sharpen: Say that percentages refer to studies, drop unsupported checklist items, and consider folding the transport and flexible-team finding into C20-05 since both rest on Forsat 2020.

scores.accuracy_concern: The self-rating was comparative ('compared with others your age'), which tends to run optimistic, so the wording must be kept on caption and visual; 'says little about how a person experiences their life' overclaims beyond what the study measured.
scores.sharpen: Replace 'says little' with a literal contrast (5 diagnoses, 3 in 4 rate health good or better) and close on the question a family can ask; schedule apart from C20-18 and C20-23.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 37% and 75% are relative overestimates, so the absolute 10-year risks must come from the full text before use; do not imply that FRAX or other common calculators share the flaw (FRAX accounts for mortality); 'benefit overstated' should be phrased as absolute benefit estimates built on the inflated baseline risk.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the absolute pair of 10-year risks and give one question to ask of any risk figure in a very old person: were deaths from other causes allowed for?

scores.accuracy_concern: Nelson and Dannefer's 65% refers to dispersion across many kinds of variables, not health alone; at the oldest ages selective survival can narrow variation, so the flat 'people differ more in health at 85 than at 50' needs hedging; the step to 'what a treatment will do' is an inference, not a finding.
scores.sharpen: Build on Lowsky's measured spread within the 85-and-over group, drop the older heterogeneity tally, and keep clear of C20-10's self-rated-health point.

scores.accuracy_concern: The HRA 'Make it Public' expectation must be quoted from an opened document (official pages may not open here); 'many trials don't share results with participants' needs a verified source.
scores.sharpen: Merge into C20-21 as one public post on taking part in research, with 'How will I hear what it found?' as the closing question.

scores.values_concern: The call to use need rather than age for services could read as a position on specific age-gated policies (pension age, screening ages, concessions); keep it to the fair-access principle and mark it as judgement.
scores.accuracy_concern: Barnett's 10 to 15 years is the population difference in onset of multimorbidity (two or more conditions) in 2007 data, not a statement about individuals; healthy life expectancy gaps need an opened source; the chart values must come from the Lancet full text.
scores.sharpen: Name one concrete age-gated entry point (a service or a trial age criterion) as the example, and keep the need-based alternative explicitly labelled as judgement.

scores.accuracy_concern: England now collects some client-level adult social care data (from 2023) and Capacity Tracker data, so 'largely missing from routine statistics' and 'as they are for other groups of NHS patients' need careful wording; every item on the counted/not counted card needs individual verification; the DACHA pilot covered 727 residents.
scores.sharpen: Lead with one verified concrete gap from DACHA (for example no routine national record of residents' function or quality of life) rather than a broad list.

scores.accuracy_concern: The claim that survivor-only averages explain studies that 'don't match clinical experience' is speculative; the illustrative diagram must be visibly marked as not data; the Kurland and Diehr methods references are unverified.
scores.sharpen: Use a real published example where a survivors-only average and an analysis including deaths diverge, if one can be verified; otherwise cut the speculative explanation and keep the two checks. Schedule apart from C20-11.

scores.accuracy_concern: If the Equality Act is mentioned, it applies in Great Britain not Northern Ireland, to adults 18 and over, with exceptions and objective justification; do not borrow Chang 2020's causal wording about ageism and health.
scores.sharpen: Include one legitimate age-linked reason (time to benefit) so readers expect some answers to differ, and drop the legal claim unless it is opened and worded exactly.

scores.accuracy_concern: Strawbridge's 50.3% is self-rated successful ageing, not self-rated health, and should not be conflated with C20-10; the WHO definition of healthy ageing must be quoted precisely from WHO 2015 or Beard 2016.
scores.sharpen: Make it practical: turn the environment half of the WHO definition into three changes a family or council can make, and schedule well apart from C20-10.

scores.accuracy_concern: 'No additional false negatives' applies to the 75-and-over non-high-probability subgroup in ADJUST-PE; the rule applies only after a non-high or unlikely clinical probability score; units are assay-dependent (FEU); NICE NG158 'consider' wording must be confirmed.
scores.sharpen: Frame it explicitly as a test threshold recalibrated for older people, the positive case of measurement fitted to the population, with the condition (over 50, after a probability score) in the first two lines.

scores.values_concern: Telling people over 85 they are more likely to die than need dialysis must read as information to guide questions, not as dismissal of their kidney care.
scores.accuracy_concern: O'Hare compared all-cause death with end-stage kidney disease, so 'more likely to die of other causes' misstates it; the cohort was US veterans, mostly men, 2007; the study covered stages 3 to 5, so the stage 3 statement needs the stage-specific figures.
scores.sharpen: Phrase the finding as 'more likely to die than to reach kidney failure needing dialysis', date and place the study, and put the three questions before the statistic.

scores.accuracy_concern: Whether Be Part of Research registration covers Scotland, and SHARE's current eligibility, need confirming from opened sources; registering does not change trial exclusion criteria, so the post should not imply it fixes under-representation.
scores.sharpen: Merge with C20-13, be exact about which register covers which nation, and keep the claim to 'being asked', not 'being included'.

scores.values_concern: Take care not to appear to belittle anti-ageism campaigning that quotes the figure; the closing ethical point should be stated as judgement.
scores.accuracy_concern: The 7.5 years is an adjusted median survival difference in 660 Ohio residents with perceptions measured up to 23 years earlier; use 'linked with', never 'because of', and do not call the figure false; keep Westerhof's 'small' effect wording exact.
scores.sharpen: Open with the figure as it is usually shared and deliver the three checks in the next lines, closing on the equal-dignity judgement.

scores.accuracy_concern: Both studies are US and from the 1990s; Tsevat measured time trade-off health values, not quality-of-life ratings, so 'rated lives lower' is loose for that study; generalising that proxy estimates 'tend to run low' needs a more recent source.
scores.sharpen: Find a recent replication or review of proxy versus self ratings in older people, describe the time trade-off result literally, and close on how to ask the person; keep clear of C20-10.

scores.accuracy_concern: Responsiveness is not validity: goal attainment scores in the trial were set and rated by clinicians, who may not have been blinded; the idea that good care 'looked ineffective because the wrong thing was measured' is speculation.
scores.sharpen: Add one line on the limitation (the people who set the goals also rate them) and make the visual a worked goal ladder with the review question.

scores.values_concern: Risks reading as language policing or slogan; the house style asks for values through specifics.
scores.accuracy_concern: A single-session change on an implicit association test does not show changed attitudes or behaviour; the claim that catastrophe framing is common in media needs a source or must go; banned phrases cannot be shown, which weakens the visual.
scores.sharpen: Recast around one concrete rewrite of a sentence type used in service reports or bids, with the experiment as modest support, or drop.

scores.accuracy_concern: Brookes 2004's 'about four times the sample size' applies to detecting an interaction of the same size as the overall effect and needs checking; the caution should run both ways, since apparent subgroup differences are also often spurious.
scores.sharpen: Use a real trial's oldest subgroup (numbers of people and events, interval width) instead of only an illustrative plot, and keep the two-way caution.

scores.accuracy_concern: Needs one specific, sourced example of a risk that rises with age; Path B must not read as encouragement to try untested treatments.
scores.sharpen: Give one real treatment where the evidence stops at a stated age, and keep it as the public counterpart of C20-26 rather than running C20-29 as well.

scores.accuracy_concern: The exact list and count of outcomes must come from Akpan 2018 (the draft opening leaves N blank); describe 'carer burden' as strain on carers; 'most services report activity' is a general claim that needs careful wording.
scores.sharpen: Open with the two outcomes readers least expect on a dashboard (loneliness, place of death) and make the visual a fill-in audit card.

scores.accuracy_concern: Han 2011 names probability, ambiguity and complexity as sources of uncertainty; that each 'calls for a different response' is judgement, and evidence on how best to communicate uncertainty is limited.
scores.sharpen: Give one sentence a clinician could say for each kind, and keep it for practitioners so it does not overlap C20-27.

scores.accuracy_concern: The comparison is adjusted and observational, and older adults who reach the service may be a selected group; crude recovery percentages must come from the full text; under-representation needs a primary source; the service described is England's, and Scottish access differs.
scores.sharpen: Give crude recovery percentages by age from the full text, one line on who gets referred, and a route for readers in Scotland.

allocation_reason: 28 of 30 candidates reach 36 with no disqualifying flag (22 reach 40, roughly 36 rescaled because the stated formula actually has a maximum of 55, not 50), and after collapsing the overlapping clusters (trial exclusion 01/05/07/09; research participation 13/21; self-rated health 10/12/18/23; uncertainty 27/29) more than 14 distinct strong ideas remain.
balance_note: The top 14 by score (22, 19, 17, 02, 06, 30, 03, 14, 11, 28, 26, 10, 24, 08) lean to practitioners: 9 practitioner, 3 public (17, 30, 10), 2 both (22, 14). To reach about 5 public posts, swap 08 for 20 (stage 3 kidney disease, public, 44) and consider 27 (public counterpart of 26, 42.5) in place of 26 or 11. The set is well balanced between criticism and teaching or good care: 19, 24, 30, 06, 26, 28 and 11 explain or show good practice.
